allow.reason: SID 0003, revision 2026-10-15 (Rust port): the reputation trie of sibuna-cidr matches the prefix 0.0.0.0/0, which the Zig trie stored but never read. With "0.0.0.0/0": "DENY" the Rust daemon denies every IPv4 client at step 2 of the evaluation order, where the Zig daemon ignored the entry. Only the configuration that loads such a policy may differ, and only by the Rust daemon denying: the status is 403.

allow.reason: Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: the WAF canonicalises fields over 8 KiB, keeps %0a for the command-injection detector, inspects bodies of binary content types, handles multipart transport padding, decodes JSON escapes and HTML entities, and closes several signature gaps; the Rust daemon therefore denies requests the Zig daemon let through or challenged, or names another WAF rule.

Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: only origin-form targets (and OPTIONS *) are accepted; an absolute-form or authority-form target gets 400 and the connection closes.

Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: paths with `;`, %2F, %5C, %00, a raw backslash, raw non-ASCII bytes or dot segments above the root get 400.

Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: paths are normalised (unreserved escapes decoded, repeated slashes merged, dot segments removed) and both the policy and the origin see the normal path, so decisions and the origin's echo follow the normal path.

Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: answers to HEAD from Sibuna's own pages carry no body; the Zig daemon wrote one, which a client reads as stray bytes after the answer.
Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: a repeated Host field gets 400.

allow.reason: Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: the trusted client address is taken --trusted-hops (default 1) entries from the right of X-Forwarded-For instead of the leftmost entry, reading all X-Forwarded-For fields as one list, so a repeated field names another client. Forward authorization trusts forwarded headers without --trust-forwarded (Config::trusts_forwarded), so every auth-* configuration is affected.

Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15), deliberately different from Zig: the trusted client address is taken --trusted-hops (default 1) entries from the right of X-Forwarded-For instead of the leftmost entry, so a list names another client. Forward authorization trusts forwarded headers without --trust-forwarded (Config::trusts_forwarded), so every auth-* configuration is affected. X-Real-IP holding a list is not an IP address and is not trusted.

allow.reason: Maintainer-approved security fix of the Rust daemon (2026-10-15, SID 0002 revision), deliberately different from Zig: a forwarded entry (X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP) that is not an IP address, such as a bracketed IPv6 address or an address with a port, is not trusted and the request is judged by the socket peer; Zig used the text as the client address.
